methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort with 604 patients (442 training, 182 validation). Machine learning models (RF, XGBoost, GBM, SVM, LR) trained with hyperparameter optimization and 5-fold cross-validation. LASSO feature selection and SHAP interpretation enhance transparency. Limitations: single-center, no external multi-center validation, JPEG images not DICOM data, low sensitivity acknowledged as critical flaw.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Diagnostic study developing prediction model for LNM in cN0 PTC. Potential to reduce unnecessary central lymph node dissection if sensitivity improved. Clinical utility currently limited by high false-negative rate (low sensitivity). Applicability contingent on addressing sensitivity-specificity trade-off.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive Methods including patient selection, ultrasound acquisition, ROI delineation, feature extraction, model construction, validation approach. Results present model performance metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity, F1, Brier), SHAP analysis, representative cases. Data availability not discussed; JPEG compression limits reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel integration of CEUS radiomics features with clinical indicators using multiple machine learning models. Achieves high AUC (0.928-0.942) for CLNM and LNM prediction, substantially exceeding prior radiomics models (AUC 0.727-0.803). SHAP visualization of feature contributions provides interpretability.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Methods enabling reproducibility (though JPEG limitation noted). Results well-organized with tables and figures demonstrating model performance. Discussion contextualizes within prior radiomics literature and acknowledges limitations transparently. SHAP visualization adds interpretability.

key_strengths: Novel integration of CEUS-derived radiomics features with clinical indicators achieving high diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.928-0.942)
Appropriate machine learning methodology with hyperparameter optimization, cross-validation, and SHAP interpretability
Honest reporting of low sensitivity limitation; authors acknowledge clinical utility currently severely compromised
LASSO feature selection and comparison of five ML algorithms strengthen robustness
key_concerns: Critically low sensitivity (insufficient to prevent missed LNM diagnoses); high specificity does not offset false-negative risk in clinical practice
Single-center retrospective design with no external validation; generalizability unknown across institutions/populations
JPEG image compression introduces artifacts; DICOM data with feature harmonization essential for multi-center studies
Manual ROI delineation by single physician without ICC assessment; observer variability unquantified
chief_reviewer.rationale: Promising radiomics-CEUS integration achieving high AUC but clinically limited by low sensitivity and high false-negative rate. Authors transparently acknowledge this limitation, preventing use as definitive diagnostic tool. Single-center design lacks external validation. Tier 3 appropriate with major revisions needed addressing sensitivity, external validation, and data harmonization.
